source.title: The Effect of Amino Acids on Wound Healing: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis on Arginine and Glutamine

primary_result_conclusion.claim: Arginine hydroxyproline and multiple glutamine outcomes significant; T-cell result not significant.

limitation_uncertainty.claim: Five arginine studies, small samples, missing arginine outcomes, high heterogeneity.

figure_table_claim.claim: SMD -0.16 (95% CI -0.33 to 0.01), totals 315 vs 312; prose reports 540 participants.

warnings.issue: Abstract hydroxyproline CI upper bound 4.45 conflicts with Results/Figure 8 upper bound 5.45.
warnings.resolution: Preserve conflict; use Figure 8/Results value 5.45 for pooled-result atom and SEA quantitative synthesis because both agree.

warnings.issue: Methods/Figures 9 and 15 identify standardized mean difference, but surrounding prose/abstract call the effect MD.
warnings.resolution: Preserve conflict; use SMD when reporting forest-plot effect measure.

warnings.issue: Figure 15 totals 315 experimental + 312 control (627) while Results prose says 540 participants.
warnings.resolution: Preserve both; figure-derived denominator is used for the Figure 15 atom.

warnings.issue: Abstract states ten electronic databases were used, while Methods explicitly names six search sources (including Google Scholar grey literature).
warnings.resolution: Report both without inventing four unlisted databases.

warnings.issue: Figures 4 and 5 contain selection counts that are not fully arithmetically reconcilable from the displayed nodes/categories.
warnings.resolution: Represent displayed counts and flag the reconciliation problem.

parsed_title: The Effect of Amino Acids on Wound Healing: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis on Arginine and Glutamine :  SEA
